clue.text: Loner male has sexual appeal?

parts.note: someone who is fit, in British slang, is attractive, so 'has sexual appeal' gives 'is fit'

explanation.surface: A question about whether a solitary man is attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfit is someone who does not belong, an outsider much like a solitary person.

clue.text: Sample rodents put back in small enclosure

indicators.note: in places the turned rodents inside the enclosure word

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

indicators.note: put back tells us the rodents are written in reverse order

parts.note: mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: A lab technician collects some rodents and returns them to a little cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns the rodents round to ECIM before they go 'in' the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is an example taken for study, the same thing as a sample.

clue.text: Radical restructuring in Washington that's thrown out head wonks

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters of the two words are tossed into disorder and reassembled

explanation.surface: Policy experts lose their jobs in a Washington purge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' rearranges HEADWONKS. 'in Washington' marks the sense as American; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a shakedown is a thorough overhaul or reorganisation of an outfit.

clue.text: Take in a pint to house party

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drink along to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a child or stray is to take it in as one's own.

clue.text: Cabinetmaker has counter roughly planed with finish in pine

parts.note: a chip is a gambling counter

indicators.note: roughly signals the letters of planed are put together loosely, in a new order
finish in points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A woodworker shapes a piece of pine with a rough planing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges PLANED to PENDAL; 'finish in' gives E, the last letter of pine. Thomas Chippendale was an 18th-century English furniture maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Chippendale was a celebrated English maker of cabinets and fine furniture.

clue.text: Title Queen bestows is returned by Republican

indicators.note: returned means the little word is to be read backwards

explanation.surface: A political party member hands back an honour the monarch conferred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns IS into SI; 'by' joins on R.
explanation.definitionFit: A knighthood, conferred by the monarch, carries the honorific used before a knight's name.

clue.text: Authorise application to travel widely

parts.note: an app is short for an application, on a phone
to rove is to wander or travel over a wide area

explanation.surface: Someone sanctions a request to go on long journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve something is to give it official sanction or authorisation.

clue.text: Closed clubs having fault in alarm

parts.note: a door that is to is shut, so closed gives to
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
a sin is a fault or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Shut nightclubs with a defect in their alarm system.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal.

clue.text: Empty power addiction and crude swagger

indicators.note: empty tells us to clear out each word's insides, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Raw power addiction and vulgar arrogance are condemned together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' keeps the outside letters of power, addiction and crude: PR, AN and CE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prance is to strut about showily, which is to swagger.

clue.text: Disadvantage with opening a religious community

parts.note: pros and cons: a con is a disadvantage
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A drawback that comes with an aperture.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent is a community of nuns living under religious vows.

clue.text: Intention to wound when cutting head

indicators.note: cutting head means removing the first letter of the word

parts.note: to maim is to wound badly

explanation.surface: Someone planning to injure by striking the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting head' removes M from MAIM; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim is an intention or purpose one sets out to achieve.

clue.text: Airborne seeds — the one here was the first found in urban area

parts.note: this means the one here, as opposed to that

indicators.note: found in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a town is an urban area
to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: The first example of windblown seed was discovered in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts the leader's verb inside the urban area, giving TLEDOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Thistledown is the fluffy material carrying thistle seeds on the wind.

clue.text: Bachelor ejected from drunken game

indicators.note: ejected from means the letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: blotto is slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: An unmarried man is thrown out of a drunken party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ejected from' removes B from BLOTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery-style game of chance, like bingo, played with numbers.

clue.text: What asthmatic might use on a trial arranged with hospital

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A patient is trying out a breathing device in a clinical trial organised with a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges ONATRIAL plus H; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler device delivers medicine to the lungs, which is what someone with asthma uses.

clue.text: Stink about skills needed for choral piece

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: pong is British slang for a bad smell
arts are skills or crafts

explanation.surface: A bad smell surrounds the talents needed for a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-song is a piece for several voices, each singing its own part.

clue.text: Courageous wordplay in something clearly blue

indicators.note: in puts one word inside the other

parts.note: on a clear day the sky is blue
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A bold joke made under clear blue skies.
explanation.definitionFit: Spunky is informal for plucky or brave, showing courage.

clue.text: One on the fiddle perhaps has problem over agents breaking in

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a sum is a maths problem

indicators.note: breaking means the agents split the little word open

parts.note: taken as written
the CIA is the American intelligence agency, its agents

explanation.surface: A fraudster is in trouble once secret agents break in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the fiddle' suggests cheating, but here it is someone playing a violin; 'over' reads the problem upwards and 'breaking' splits the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist plays a fiddle, and is one example of someone who plays an instrument.

clue.text: Hindu mystic floated above one

parts.note: swam means floated or moved through water
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A levitating holy man hovering over a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' places SWAM before I.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or ascetic.

clue.text: What's starting in rage and exasperation?

definitions.text: What's starting in rage and exasperation?

indicators.note: starting points to the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A question about what begins when someone is furious and exasperated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes I, R and E from in, rage and exasperation; the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger, the very feeling found in rage and exasperation.

clue.text: Hanging has to finish in a gasp

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath
to end is to finish

explanation.surface: Someone choking on the gallows has to die gasping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' suggests the gallows, but the answer is a noun for a hanging ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is a piece of jewellery that hangs, so a hanging ornament.

clue.text: Period of recovery after abandoning new version for merger

indicators.note: after abandoning means the named letters have been dropped from the word

parts.note: convalescence is the time spent recovering from illness

explanation.surface: A recovering patient gives up a new version to merge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after abandoning' removes N and V from CONVALESCENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Coalescence is the coming together of parts into one, a merging.

clue.text: Show bottom part of leg beneath the knee and note rot

parts.note: to moon is to show one's bare bottom

parts.words: part of leg beneath the knee
parts.note: the shin is the front of the leg below the knee
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone exposes their behind and their lower leg, while a note is decaying.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine means foolish talk or nonsense, as does rot.

clue.text: Zero attempt to involve a legal functionary

parts.note: no means none, zero

indicators.note: to involve means the attempt word wraps round the letter

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: No attempt is made to bring in a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is an official authorised to witness and certify legal documents.

clue.text: No country dweller has to confess when breaking limit

indicators.note: breaking means the confessing word bursts into the limit word

parts.note: to tie is to restrict or limit
to own up is to confess, so to own is to admit

explanation.surface: A city dweller who has to admit to crossing a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A townie is a person from a town, the opposite of someone from the countryside.

clue.text: Having jaw extended messed up gnash or pout

indicators.note: messed up signals the letters of these words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grinding teeth and sulking with a jutting jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messed up' rearranges GNASHORPOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Prognathous is the anatomical term for having a protruding jaw.

clue.text: A sheep kept penned within safe boundary

indicators.note: kept penned within means one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep is held in a fold within a safe perimeter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept penned within' puts ARAM inside PETER, after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A parameter is a limit or boundary within which something operates.

clue.text: Large fish of burn and stream

parts.note: a sting is a sharp burning pain
a ray is a stream or beam of light

explanation.surface: A big fish of the Scottish brook and river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' suggests a Scottish stream, but here it means a sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a large flat fish with a venomous tail spine.

clue.text: Incitement to rebellion eliminating head of state and issue

indicators.note: eliminating means a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: sedition is speech or action stirring rebellion

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Rebels plotting to remove the head of state, and the question at stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives S from state; 'eliminating' removes it from SEDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one printed issue of a newspaper or book.

clue.text: Carbon yacht redesigned with instant appeal

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

indicators.note: redesigned signals the letters of the boat word are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A carbon-fibre yacht is remodelled to look attractive at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges YACHT to ATCHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something catchy, like a tune, is immediately appealing and memorable.

clue.text: Bitterness over work and career

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: gall is bitterness or resentment
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A resentful person looks back at work and their professional life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun for a job, but it is the verb to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush headlong, much as a horse at full speed would.

clue.text: In many instances temper starts too late

indicators.note: starts too late means the word is missing its opening letter

parts.note: to soften is to temper or moderate

explanation.surface: Often a person loses their temper only after starting too late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts too late' drops the S from SOFTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, on many occasions.

clue.text: Polish drink

definitions.meaning: to polish gems or glass with a rotating wheel
to drink like a cat, with the tongue

explanation.definitionFit: A lap is a polishing wheel, and to lap up liquid is to drink it.
